ming:
Use case: stylized-concept. Production transparent pixel-art animation atlas for a teaching simulator. The attached image is the character identity and pixel style reference. Create EXACTLY 8 columns and 6 rows of equally sized square cells, 48 frames, no borders, no text. Each cell has the SAME boy Ming: purple messy hair and round purple glasses, mint collared shirt, lilac shorts and sneakers, seated at a honey-colored desk with purple chair, open notebook and pencil. Crisp detailed pixel art, consistent face, large cute head. Transparent background.
CRITICAL animation registration: same orthographic front camera, same scale, desk perfectly stationary at identical coordinates in every cell, feet on same baseline, whole furniture inside every cell with margins. Reserve space above head for standing.
Row 1 (8 frames): dozing animation, start attentive, eyelids droop, eyes shut, head dips gradually to lowest at frame4, nod, startled eyes open, recover to initial attentive pose.
Row 2 (8 frames): confused animation, attentive, slight head tilt, stronger tilt, hand starts rising, hand touches hair scratching, lower hand, recover, attentive.
Row 3 (8 frames): writing: first4 reaching for pencil and bringing to book, next4 small continuous writing strokes on notebook.
Row 4 (8 frames): first4 putting pencil down and returning hand; last4 attentive blink and reading.
Row 5 (8 frames): smooth sit-to-stand rising behind desk: seated then hands on desk, hips rise, knees straighten, gradually become fully standing by eighth frame. Furniture stays fixed, feet remain grounded.
Row 6 (8 frames): first2 standing behind desk mouth closed/open (only mouth changes); next6 smooth lowering from standing to seated, ending exact attentive starting pose.
Avoid pose jitter, shifting desk, extra characters, numbers, labels, antialiased vector look.
